title: Stripes and dots without images
summary: repeating-linear-gradient for stripes; a small radial-gradient tile repeated for dots.
explanation: Hard colour stops make a gradient change colour abruptly instead of blending: #fed7aa 0 10px, #fff 10px 20px is 10px of orange then 10px of white. repeating-linear-gradient repeats that band forever, giving stripes.

The dots are one radial-gradient: a 3px orange circle that turns transparent right after. background-size: 20px 20px makes that a 20px tile, and background-repeat (repeat, the default) tiles it across the box.
Both are plain backgrounds, so they scale and recolour without any image file.
tryThis: Change 45deg to 90deg in .stripes for vertical stripes.
Change background-size in .dots to 12px 12px: a denser grid.
Set background-repeat: no-repeat on .dots: only one dot remains, in the top-left corner.
